title: Slices
description:
Return slices that point into the input instead of building new strings or vectors:

```rust
fn first_word(text: &str) -> &str          // up to the first space; the whole text if there is none
fn last_word(text: &str) -> &str           // after the last space, ignoring trailing spaces
fn trim_zeros(values: &[i32]) -> &[i32]    // without leading and trailing zeros
fn max_window_sum(values: &[i32], k: usize) -> Option<i32>   // the largest sum of k neighbours; None if k is 0 or too big
fn split_on(values: &[i32], separator: i32) -> Vec<&[i32]>   // like str::split, for numbers
```

`split_on(&[1, 0, 2, 3, 0, 0, 4], 0)` gives `[[1], [2, 3], [], [4]]`.
hints: `text.trim_end()` removes white space from the end only. `text.find(' ')` and `text.rfind(' ')` (which searches from the end) give byte positions; `&text[..i]` and `&text[i + 1..]` slice around them.
`values.windows(k)` yields every run of `k` neighbours as a slice; sum each with `window.iter().sum::<i32>()`.
